assembly_notes: Quarter-turn butterfly valve. The grounded `valve_body` part is a real ring: a CadQuery annulus on the pipe axis with a seat liner inside it, a stem tower bored for the stem, and a notched locking quadrant under the operator. The `rotor` carries the disc and the stem and turns REVOLUTE about +z from shut to open across a quarter turn; the disc radius is the bore minus a 0.8 mm running clearance, so the swept envelope stays inside the liner at every angle. Four slots vary without touching that chain. body_end makes the ends off - drilled bolt-ear lugs, raised drilled flanges, or machined coupling grooves with clamp segments - and all three put flange_bolt_count features on the same derived bolt circle. disc_form varies the disc between a flat concentric plate, an offset high-performance disc with a profiled sealing edge, an eccentric double-offset plate on its own hub boss, and a revolved conical triple-offset disc that tapers from hub to rim. operator varies the input between a trigger lever riding the quadrant, a transverse tee bar with two grips, and a worm gearbox whose handwheel turns CONTINUOUS on its own horizontal input axis; the first two are FIXED to the rotor and turn with the disc. bonnet_form sets how far the operator boss stands above the body - straight off the short cast tower, or on a tall extended neck column with its own gussets - and every operator, quadrant and stem length derives from that one height. bore_radius_m, face_to_face_m and operator_reach_m are honest continuous parameters; palette and notch counts are non-core.
